notes:
Summary: Large payments processor evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) to host inference pipelines for fraud scoring, customer chat, and document embeddings. Main ask: enterprise-grade audit logging and SIEM export + BYOK KMS integration.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2026-02-10: Intro call (AE Samantha) — high level requirements captured.
- 2026-02-18: Security intake form submitted; security team requested detailed log schema.
- 2026-02-25: Tech deep-dive w/ SE (Ravi) — discussed deployment model (VPC peering + private control plane) and threat model.
- 2026-03-02: Recorded call (Fireflies ff_20260302_9871) — requested sample audit logs, retention policy.
- 2026-03-09: Follow-up with Infra/Sec to review SIEM connector options (ff_20260309_1024).
- POC status: small lab deployed in customer VPC; running synthetic traffic to validate prefix caching and request tracing.

Audit logging & SIEM export requirements (customer-specified):
- All inference request/response metadata must be logged (structured JSON). No free-form text allowed in admin logs.
- Exports: primary requirement is push to Splunk HEC; fallback/alternatives: S3 bucket (encrypted), Kafka topic (TLS + SASL), syslog over TLS to customer's SIEM appliance, or native Elastic ingest pipeline.
- Transport security: TLS1.2+, mutual TLS option for syslog; signed JWTs for HTTP deliveries; support for proxy/VPN endpoints in restricted networks.
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once acceptable, but prefer idempotent delivery support and sequence tokens to avoid duplication in SIEM.

Log schema (requested fields; customer will add additional columns):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- request_id (uuid)
- account_id (customer tenant id)
- model_id
- model_version
- route_name (api route)
- user_id (pseudonymized)
- prompt_hash (sha256)
- token_count_input
- token_count_output
- latency_ms
- server_node (k8s pod / instance id)
- client_ip (redacted per residency policy)
- decision_flags (e.g., reranked, cached_prefix_hit)
- error_code / status
- auth_method (token | mTLS | sso)
- kms_key_id (if any)
- tenant_region
- retention_tier (hot|cold|archive)

- Example (single-line JSON): {"timestamp":"2026-03-09T14:23:05Z","request_id":"a1b2c3","account_id":"meridian-tenant-9","model_id":"gpt-small-v2","latency_ms":312,"token_count_input":42,"token_count_output":128,"server_node":"ip-10-0-3-21"}

Retention & lifecycle policy (customer constraints):
- Regulatory requirement: retain full audit trail for 7 years for transaction-scoped requests.
- Hot/warm/cold tiers: 90 days hot (readily queryable), 1 year warm, remainder archived to WORM-capable storage (S3 Glacier or equivalent) for years 2-7.
- Deletion requests: must support targeted deletion for specific PII-bearing request_ids (subject to legal review).
- Encryption-at-rest: customer BYOK required for archive; keys in their HSM/KMS and audited key-usage logs exported.

Access logs & admin audit:
- Admin console actions to be logged: role changes, API key creation/rotation, model rollout/rollback, configuration changes to routing policies, KMS key bindings.
- Logs must include actor (SSO identifier), timestamp, IP, user agent, and before/after config diffs where applicable.
- Emergency access sessions (jump-host style) must generate session transcripts exportable to SIEM.

KMS / BYOK specifics:
- Customer requires HSM-backed keys (AWS CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM / on-prem HSM).
- Redwood Private must support key wrapping/unwrapping hooks and produce key-usage audit events to the same SIEM stream. Key rotation events should be explicit in logs.
- Requirement: never persist plaintext customer keys on Redwood-managed control plane; all key ops executed in customer VPC or via KMIP/HSM broker.

Operational expectations & SLOs: 
- Redwood to provide a log-forwarding SLA: 99.5% successful delivery of events to configured SIEM endpoint within 30s for hot-tier events.
- Ability to replay logs for a 7-day window from internal archival to recover from transient delivery outages.

Security review notes / quotes: 
- Security lead: "We need deterministic, structured logs we can query — nothing free-text in main audit stream."
- Compliance: must map to internal evidence buckets for PCI / FFIEC.

Open questions / risks called out by customer: 
- How will prompt/response content be redacted or hashed before logging to meet data residency rules?
- Can Redwood support per-route retention rules (e.g., support-agent logs 90 days, fraud-scoring 7 years)?
- Validation of Splunk HEC token rotation without downtime.

Next steps (action items):
- AE/Sec: deliver SIEM export spec draft by 2026-03-12 (drive://meridian/sec/siem-export-spec.xlsx).
- SE (Ravi): provide sample 1M log/day ingestion cost estimate and recommended shard/partitioning for Kafka path.
- Legal + Customer: start BYOK policy review (ticket SEC-7830).
- Schedule onsite SOC/Q review w/ customer compliance 2026-03-20.

Short notes / CRM shorthand: 
- Priority: P1 for infra/compliance teams.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high (wants Optimize to tune token throughput).
- Demo ask: show log-forwarding to Splunk + S3 archival + KMS key-usage events.
- "If we can't get deterministic logs to Splunk, won't sign" — Head of Compliance.
public_notes: Evaling Redwood Private for VPC-deployed inference. SIEM export + BYOK KMS = gating. Splunk HEC primary target; need retention 7yrs and per-route retention rules. SE Ravi building sample ingest. Legal reviewing BYOK.
sales_pitch: Position Redwood Private as secure, auditable inference runtime: structured JSON audit logs, multi-destination SIEM export (Splunk/Kafka/S3), BYOK/KMS integrations with HSM support, and configurable retention tiers. Emphasize per-route retention and admin audit trails for compliance evidence.
technical_summary: Customer requires structured audit logs with fields for request tracing, model_id/version, latency, token counts, and KMS key identifiers. Exports must support Splunk HEC, syslog over mTLS, Kafka, and S3 with encryption. Retain 7 years with hot/warm/archive tiers. Admin console and key events must be included.
